catalyst_text: Initiated Phase 1 single ascending dose obesity study
detailed_catalyst_text: A Phase 1 single-ascending-dose, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in healthy adults with BMI ≥30 was initiated to assess safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics. The start followed FDA clearance of an IND, marking a key regulatory and clinical step for a DACRA being developed for weight loss.
catalyst_text_evidence: SAN DIEGO, 2026-06-24 /PRNewswire/ -- Viking Therapeutics, Inc. ("Viking") (NASDAQ:VKTX), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the development of novel therapies for metabolic and endocrine disorders, announced today the initiation of a Phase 1 single ascending dose (SAD) clinical trial of VK3019, an investigational dual amylin and calcitonin receptor agonist (DACRA). The study initiation follows the filing and clearance of VK3019's investigational new drug (IND) application with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The Phase 1 trial is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled SAD study in healthy adults with BMI ≥30.

catalyst_text: Presented positive data and Phase 3 baseline demographics
detailed_catalyst_text: The company presented additional results from a Phase 2 oral study showing significant, dose-dependent weight loss over 13 weeks in adults with obesity or overweight. A second poster presented the design and enrollment demographics of the ongoing Phase 3 VANQUISH-1 study of the subcutaneous formulation in adults with obesity or overweight with comorbidities. These presentations provide supportive efficacy data and context for the registrational program.
catalyst_text_evidence: Viking Therapeutics, Inc. ... today presented additional data from its Phase 2 VENTURE-Oral Dosing trial evaluating the oral tablet formulation of VK2735 at the European Congress on Obesity (ECO) in Istanbul, Türkiye. Participants receiving once-daily oral VK2735 demonstrated statistically significant, dose-dependent weight loss from baseline of up to 12.2% (26.6 lbs) at 13 weeks across all dose cohorts. Viking also presented a second poster at ECO today highlighting the design and enrollment demographics of the ongoing Phase 3 VANQUISH-1 study of subcutaneous VK2735 in adults with obesity or who are overweight and have at least one weight-related comorbidity.

catalyst_text: Completed enrollment in Phase 3 obesity trial
detailed_catalyst_text: Enrollment was completed in the Phase 3 VANQUISH-1 trial evaluating once-weekly subcutaneous dosing in adults with obesity or who are overweight. This milestone advances the registrational program toward pivotal outcomes.
catalyst_text_evidence: Concurrently, Viking is conducting the Phase 3 VANQUISH-1 study of subcutaneous VK2735 in patients who have obesity or are overweight. Enrollment in VANQUISH-1 was completed in November 2025.

catalyst_text: Completed enrollment in Phase 3 obesity diabetes trial
detailed_catalyst_text: Patient enrollment was completed for the Phase 3 VANQUISH-2 trial in adults with type 2 diabetes who have obesity or are overweight. The 78-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study assesses percent change in body weight, marking key progress in the registrational program.
catalyst_text_evidence: SAN DIEGO, 2026-03-26 /PRNewswire/ -- Viking Therapeutics, Inc. (Viking) (NASDAQ:VKTX), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the development of novel therapies for metabolic and endocrine disorders, today announced the completion of patient enrollment in its Phase 3 VANQUISH-2 clinical trial of subcutaneous VK2735, the company's dual agonist of the glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptors. The trial enrolled approximately 1,000 adults with type 2 diabetes and who have obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2) or who are overweight (BMI ≥27 kg/m2).

catalyst_text: Completed enrollment in Phase 3 obesity overweight trial
detailed_catalyst_text: Enrollment was completed in the VANQUISH-1 Phase 3 trial assessing weekly subcutaneous dosing over 78 weeks in adults with obesity or overweight. About 4,650 participants were enrolled in this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study across multiple dose arms.
catalyst_text_evidence: In addition to the maintenance dosing study, Viking is currently conducting two Phase 3 studies evaluating subcutaneous VK2735 (VANQUISH-1 and VANQUISH-2). These trials are randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trials designed to assess the efficacy and safety of subcutaneous VK2735 dosed weekly for 78 weeks. The VANQUISH-1 study has completed enrollment of approximately 4,650 adults with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2) or who are overweight (BMI ≥27 kg/m2) with at least one weight-related co-morbid condition.

catalyst_text: Completed enrollment in Phase 1 maintenance trial
detailed_catalyst_text: Enrollment was completed for a Phase 1 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled maintenance dosing study in adults with obesity (BMI ≥30). Approximately 180 otherwise healthy adults were enrolled to evaluate safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and exploratory weight outcomes across subcutaneous and oral maintenance regimens following initial weekly treatment.
catalyst_text_evidence: Viking Therapeutics, Inc. (Viking) (NASDAQ:VKTX), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the development of novel therapies for metabolic and endocrine disorders, today announced the completion of patient enrollment in its exploratory maintenance dosing study of VK2735, the company's dual agonist of the glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptors. The maintenance dosing study is a Phase 1, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial designed to evaluate various dosing regimens, following initial weight loss achieved with weekly VK2735 treatment. The trial enrolled approximately 180 adults with BMI ≥30 kg/m2 but who are otherwise healthy.

detailed_catalyst_text: Viking completed patient enrollment in the Phase 3 VANQUISH-1 trial evaluating subcutaneous VK2735 in adults with obesity or overweight with comorbidities. This milestone advances the 78-week randomized, placebo-controlled study toward topline efficacy and safety results assessing percent change in body weight.
catalyst_text_evidence: "We are excited to announce completion of enrollment in VANQUISH-1 ahead of schedule," said Brian Lian, Ph.D., chief executive officer of Viking. The trial enrolled approximately 4,650 adults with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2) or who are overweight (BMI ≥27 kg/m2) with at least one weight-related co-morbid condition. The primary endpoint of the trial is the percent change in body weight from baseline for participants receiving VK2735 as compared to placebo after 78 weeks of treatment.

catalyst_text: Results from an exploratory analysis of Viking's Phase 2 VENTURE trial of VK2735 were presented in a poster at ObesityWeek on 2025-11-06. After 13 weeks of weekly subcutaneous VK2735, 78% of patients who were prediabetic at baseline shifted to normal glycemic status versus 29% for placebo (p=0.0008). Additionally, 68% of patients with metabolic syndrome at baseline no longer met MetS criteria at Week 13 versus 38% for placebo (p=0.02). These data indicate VK2735 improved cardiometabolic parameters in the 13-week study.
